clue.text: Sleeping by centre of furnace, I? Not at all

definitions.text: Sleeping by centre of furnace, I? Not at all

parts.note: someone sleeping is abed, in bed

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter, taken from furnace here

parts.note: the self that says I is the ego

explanation.surface: Someone dozing beside a fiery furnace insists they feel nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: in the Book of Daniel this companion of Shadrach and Meshach was thrown into the fiery furnace and was not burnt at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible story, one of three Hebrews cast into Nebuchadnezzar's furnace who emerged unharmed.

clue.text: Horse the French deemed suitable for ploughing

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A French horse is judged fit to pull a plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Land fit for growing crops, able to be tilled.

clue.text: Wild rose could be elegant in arrangement

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wild rose would look elegant in a flower arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet briar, a wild rose of European hedgerows.

clue.text: Six counties confusable with new one, initially?

definitions.text: Six counties confusable with new one, initially?

parts.words: Six counties confusable with new one, initially?
parts.note: the region of six counties has the initials N I, the same as the initials of new one

explanation.surface: Six counties that might be mistaken for a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The six counties are the part of the UK in the north-east of Ireland; its abbreviation NI matches the first letters of new one.
explanation.definitionFit: The six counties of Ulster that remain part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Tear newspaper up revealing who created Perry Mason

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rend is to tear
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Ripping up a newspaper reveals the writer behind a famous fictional lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REND RAG backwards. Erle Stanley ___ wrote the Perry Mason courtroom novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The American crime novelist who wrote the Perry Mason lawyer stories.

clue.text: Smuggler's'good for the resistance, one's sure to have weapon

indicators.note: G for good is put in place of R, the physics symbol for resistance

parts.note: a runner is a smuggler, as in rum-runner or gun-runner

explanation.surface: A smuggler aids an armed resistance movement, every member of which is sure to carry a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An artilleryman or anyone firing a gun is by definition armed.

clue.text: Labour scorn utter dunce not converted to current political ways

definitions.text: not converted to current political ways

indicators.note: to labour material is to work it over, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: The Labour Party scorns an utter dunce who refuses to modernise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party; it signals that SCORN UTTER DUNCE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding old-fashioned views, unreformed and unwilling to adopt modern attitudes.

clue.text: Innocent one taking refuge in part of church

indicators.note: the numeral for one shelters inside the church part

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An innocent person seeks sanctuary in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated and lacking worldly experience, artless.

clue.text: Change order pertaining to anaesthetic

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
an anaesthetic makes you number, more numb

explanation.surface: A doctor changes the order of a prescription for anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anaesthetic' looks like a noun, but read as producing numbness it gives NUMBER, more numb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign fresh numerals in a new sequence.

clue.text: A copper people follow for keen insight

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men are people

explanation.surface: A policeman followed by a crowd shows sharp insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman; it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness, the ability to make quick sharp judgements.

clue.text: Comparatively skilful Ibsen character, but not the lead

indicators.note: the lead is the opening letter, which is dropped from the surname

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title character of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: An actor more skilful than most gets an Ibsen role, though not the starring part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lead' sounds like the leading role in the play, but it means the first letter of the character's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: More able is the comparative of able, meaning skilful.

clue.text: Run course in tricky mathematical procedure

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Running a course in some tricky bit of maths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is the cricket R, a convention worth knowing; the surface suggests jogging a training course, but the definition is the computing and maths sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A process defined in terms of itself, applied repeatedly, as in computing or mathematics.

clue.text: Hard getting a number after worker's on line at no.57?

indicators.note: in an across clue, the worker sitting on the line means it comes to the right of it
after places the pencil-hard letter, a and number behind the worker on the line

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's usual worker
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A hard worker standing on a line at house number 57 gets a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no.57' is the atomic number: this rare-earth element is number 57 in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical element with atomic number fifty-seven, first of the rare-earth series.

clue.text: Defeat for American elite

definitions.meaning: in American slang, to ... a team is to beat it soundly
the best part of anything, like the top of the milk

explanation.definitionFit: US slang for thrashing an opponent, and also the pick of a group, skimmed off the top.

clue.text: What may be seen in reflecting telescope daily?

definitions.text: What may be seen in reflecting telescope
definitions.meaning: a reflecting telescope gathers light with a curved glass reflector
a British daily tabloid newspaper of this name

explanation.definitionFit: A reflecting glass is the key optic of such a telescope, and it is also a British tabloid paper published daily.

clue.text: Girl who's after something not acceptable in musical?

definitions.text: Girl who's after something not acceptable in musical?

parts.words: Girl who's after something not acceptable in musical?
parts.note: the 1925 musical comedy title puts the heroine's name after two refusals, a no-no being something not acceptable

explanation.surface: A girl in a show chases something forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: The title heroine of the musical No, No, ___, whose name follows a no-no.

clue.text: As a key operator who's level-headed must do?

definitions.text: As a key operator who's level-headed must do?

parts.words: As a key operator who's level-headed must do?
parts.note: a typist who keeps the head level, eyes on the copy rather than looking down at the keys, works by feel

explanation.surface: A calm keyholder must act as expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To type using all fingers by feel, without looking at the keyboard.

clue.text: Desires to have no unknown income

indicators.note: Y is an algebraic unknown, and it is dropped

parts.note: yearnings are strong desires

explanation.surface: Wanting to have no unknown sources of income.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, so 'unknown' can be Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Money received as wages or profit.

clue.text: Fish porter's mate

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
a mate is a spouse, such as a wife

explanation.surface: A railway porter's wife cooks fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a man carrying bags; it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American herring-like fish; the word also once meant a woman keeping an alehouse.

clue.text: Have high regard for hunt gatherings English set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a meet is a gathering of a fox hunt

explanation.surface: The English set up hunt meetings for those they admire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns MEETS E backwards. A meet is where riders and hounds assemble before a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire and respect someone greatly.

clue.text: Inconvenience, changing parts for production

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase swap places

parts.note: to inconvenience someone is to put them out

explanation.surface: Changing the components of a factory line is an inconvenience to production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing parts' swaps the two words of PUT OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Output is the amount produced by a factory or worker.

clue.text: Be on top of extra song that's endless

parts.note: over means extra, left over

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: Singing an extra song that never ends puts you on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie upon or cover something else.

clue.text: Some racking periods at the wicket

definitions.meaning: frames or racks for holding things, such as hat or music holders
in cricket, a batsman's time at the crease or a partnership

explanation.definitionFit: Racks for hats or umbrellas, and in cricket the spells two batsmen spend together at the crease.

clue.text: King wearing uniform's given backing for bravery

indicators.note: the king is clothed by, so set inside, the reversed word
backing means the word for uniform is read backwards

parts.note: uniform as an adjective means even, the same throughout
R is short for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A king in uniform receives support for his courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given backing' turns EVEN into NEVE, and 'wearing' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is courage or daring in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Wander strangely without clothing?

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word, on either side, are stripped away like garments

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about oddly wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without clothing' strips ST from the front and LY from the back of strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam or travel freely over an area.

clue.text: Military machine that could spell the end for Robert the Bruce?

indicators.note: spell here hints that the letters may be rearranged to spell something else
the end of a word is its last letter, taken from Robert

explanation.surface: A siege engine that might have finished off the Scottish king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could spell' rearranges THE BRUCE into TREBUCHE, and 'end for' takes the T closing Robert. Robert the Bruce was a medieval Scottish king who besieged English-held castles.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval siege engine, a counterweighted catapult hurling stones at castle walls.

clue.text: Nothing about production of new opera is unique

indicators.note: about puts nil around the rearranged letters

parts.note: nil means nothing, as in a football score

indicators.note: a production of an opera reworks it, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Nothing in this new opera production is original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' signals the anagram; 'about' says nil goes round the scrambled letters, splitting after its first letter. The surface picture of an opera staging hides the dictionary word for peerless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peerless or without equal, unmatched by anything else.

clue.text: Experiment with new clothing in attempt to deceive

definitions.meaning: to test garments by putting them on
British slang for a bluff or chancy deception

explanation.definitionFit: Testing garments before buying, and British slang for a cheeky bid to fool someone.

clue.text: Second toy bear suggested for girlfriend, perhaps

indicators.note: suggested means the sound of the pieces hints at the word, not the spelling

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for second; a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A boy gives his girlfriend a second teddy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus TEDDY, said together, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular romantic partner, such as a girlfriend.

clue.text: Provokes saint that's uncalled for

parts.note: to needle someone is to provoke or irritate them

explanation.surface: Someone who taunts a saint does so unnecessarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnecessary, not required by circumstances.
